summary: Finland charges non-EU/EEA students tuition for English-taught degrees, but the University of Helsinki — Finland's largest and highest-ranked university — waives half or all of it for excellent applicants. Each master's programme can also award one Finland Scholarship.
covers: A tuition-fee waiver of 50% or 100%. Master's fees are €13,000, €15,000 or €18,000 a year depending on the programme, so the waiver is worth up to €36,000 over two years.
Most awards are 50% waivers; full waivers are few.
One Finland Scholarship per master's programme for a newly admitted student, which adds a €5,000 grant to the waiver in the first year.
Waivers run for two years if you make full-time progress (at least 55 ECTS credits a year). They do not pay living costs.
eligibility: Citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who are liable for tuition fees (those without permanent EU/EEA residence).
Excellent results in previous studies — the scholarship is merit-based and decided by each programme.
Admission to an English-taught master's programme at the University of Helsinki.
how_to_apply: Choose up to the permitted number of master's programmes and check each one's entry requirements.
Apply for the programme and the scholarship on the same online application form — tick the scholarship option.
Upload your degree certificates, transcripts, language certificate and any programme-specific documents by the application deadline (the main round closes in early January).
Scholarship decisions arrive with, or shortly after, the admission results in spring.
watch_out: Plan your budget around a 50% waiver unless you are told otherwise — a full waiver is the exception.
Finnish residence permits require proof of funds for living costs, separate from tuition.
You must keep a full-time pace (55 ECTS a year) or you lose the waiver in year two.
